mcpEnableNote: Serves the open API, MCP and the skill on this computer: agents can list groups and hosts, open SSH connections and run commands.

mcpRiskIntro: Read these risks before you turn it on:
mcpRiskCommands: Any program on this computer that has the access token can list your hosts and run any command on them, including deleting data or shutting a server down.
mcpRiskNoAsk: Commands from the open API, MCP or the skill do not go through the AI permission modes. They run without asking you and are only recorded in the AI audit log.
mcpRiskInjection: An agent can be steered by prompt injection in web pages, files or command output into running commands you never asked for.
mcpRiskSecrets: Passwords, keys and passphrases are never sent to agents. Hosts that need one typed are refused.
mcpRiskLocal: The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Keep the token secret, make a new one if it leaks, and turn the server off when you don’t need it.

aiDefaultModelNote: Fetch the provider’s chat models to choose from, or type a model name. Each pane can switch to another model.
aiFetchedModels: {count, plural, one {Found # chat model} other {Found # chat models}}
aiParamsNote: A parameter is sent only while it is ticked. Otherwise the provider’s default applies.
aiLegacyTokens: Send the limit as max_tokens (older endpoints)
aiAnthropicTokensNote: The Anthropic format requires a limit. {limit} is sent while it is unticked.
aiAttachUnsupported: “{name}” can’t be attached: only images, PDFs and text files can.
aiAttachTextOnly: “{name}” can’t be attached: this agent reads text files only.
aiAttachTooMany: A question can carry at most {count} files.
aiAuditUnavailable: The AI audit log is unavailable, so the command was not run: {reason}
aiAuditRecordFailed: The command ran, but its audit record could not be saved: {reason}
aiReviewProviderNote: In Review mode, read-only operations run, critical ones always ask you, and the selected model checks the rest against your requests; only explicit approval runs it, otherwise you are asked.
aiReviewModelNote: Leave empty to use the provider's default model.
aiReviewStrictnessNote: How sure the decision model must be that an action is safe: loose 80%, standard 90%, strict 97%.
aiTypeSafeNote: TypeSafe providers make review decisions only and are not offered in panes.
aiEmptyTerminal: Answers draw on this tab’s terminal. The assistant works by typing into it, with no file access; what it types follows the permission below.
aiACPNeedsSSH: External agents need an SSH host. Switch to the built-in assistant to work in this terminal.
aiReviewDeclined: The review model declined to judge this action
filesPaneBusy: The files pane of this tab is still transferring. Finish or cancel its transfers first.
aiPaneBusy: The AI assistant of this tab is still working. Stop it first.
aiClearChatBody: Its messages are removed from this pane and from this host's chat history. This cannot be undone.
aiHistoryEmpty: No saved chats on this host yet
aiAgentForgot: The agent does not remember the chat above. Your next question starts a new session.
aiHistorySaveFailed: Could not save this chat to the host's history
aiDeleteChatBody: It is removed from this host's chat history. This cannot be undone.
scpFallbackNote: This server has no SFTP: files move with scp and shell commands. An upload is sent once it is complete.
schemeImportNote: An .itermcolors file, as the iTerm2-Color-Schemes collection publishes them. You can also drop it on the schemes above.
palettePlaceholder: Search commands, settings, hosts and snippets…
shortcutRecordHint: Press the new shortcut. Esc cancels.
shortcutKeyInvalid: Use a letter, digit, punctuation or function key.
shortcutNeedsMods: The shortcut must hold {mods}, so other keys reach the shell.
shortcutReserved: {keys} belongs to the system or to editing text.

migrationDesc: Import SSH sessions from configuration files and client exports
migrationReadOnly: Source files are read only; review selections and warnings before saving
migrationReadError: Cannot read source files; check the paths and file permissions
migrationSaveSecrets: Save available credentials in the encrypted local store
migrationSecretsNote: Off by default; encrypted or unavailable source credentials must be entered again
migrationConflict: Duplicate address, port and user; choose how to handle it
migrationDependency: An invalid session or unresolved jump dependency prevents saving; correct the selection
migrationStale: Saved hosts changed after preview; close this preview and read the source again
migrationSaveError: Could not save the migration; no successful import is reported
migrationKeyError: Cannot read this key or passphrase; choose a local key, correct its passphrase or disable credentials for this row
migrationEncryptedSecret: Encrypted credential cannot be transferred; enter it again after import
migrationInvalidEntry: Invalid SSH session; deselect it before saving
migrationDuplicateID: Duplicate source identifier; resolve the source before importing this session
migrationJumpCount: Jump dependencies: {count}; all must resolve before saving
migrationFormatError: Unsupported or damaged export; choose the matching source and export format
migrationTooLarge: Source exceeds the limit of 32 MiB or 1,024 files; select a smaller batch
migrationEncryptedSource: This export is encrypted; export an unencrypted connection configuration and try again
migrationTextInput: Enter or paste a host list
migrationTextHelp: One host per line, as key=value fields separated by spaces: host or ip, port, user or username, password, and title, name or label for the name. authType is ignored and a missing password stays blank. Quote a value with spaces, as in title="web 01".
migrationUnclosedQuote: Unclosed quote; the rest of the line became this value
migrationInvalidHost: Enter a host name or IP address without a port, user or spaces
migrationFixRows: {count} hosts need attention; correct the fields marked in red
localKeysRefused: Tried {count} keys on this computer; the server accepted none.
rememberKeyPassphraseHint: Saved encrypted on this computer once it logs in; never included in backups.
localKeysTryNote: Hosts set to Auto log in with the SSH agent and the keys in ~/.ssh first, and ask for the password only if none works.
localKeysMCPNote: AI agents connecting through MCP may log in to Auto hosts with these keys without asking. Encrypted keys need a remembered passphrase.
toolPanesNote: Replace shows one tool at a time in its place; Side by side keeps every tool you open, opening the ones past three, or with no room beside, under those already open
filesEdgeNote: Where the files pane opens beside the terminal
openLocalOnStartNote: Open a local terminal when SSHYard starts
terminalFallbackFontNote: Draws CJK and other characters the terminal font lacks
rightClickNote: Copy or paste copies the selection, or pastes without one. Shift-right-click always opens the menu.
copyOnSelectNote: Text selected in the terminal is copied to the clipboard
pathPlaceholder: A path, ~/ for home, or a folder here
outputEncodingTip: Output encoding: {encoding}; affects new output only, re-run commands to refresh history
terminalEncodingHint: New terminals of this host decode output with this encoding.
errSerialNotFound: {device} isn’t connected. Plug in the device or choose another port.
errSerialBusy: {device} is in use by another program.
errSerialPermission: Not allowed to open {device}. On Linux, add your user to the dialout group.
monitorStream: Metrics need SSH. This pane is a Telnet or serial terminal.
autoLoginHint: SSHYard answers the login and password prompts for you.
noSerialPorts: No serial ports found. Type the device name instead.
localEchoHint: Show what you type when the other end doesn’t echo it.
telnetPlaintext: Telnet is unencrypted: everything, passwords included, crosses the network in plain text. Use it only on networks you trust.
jumpNotSSH: Jump hosts must be SSH hosts.
forwardNotSSH: Port forwards go through SSH hosts only.
credentialPasswordOnly: Telnet and serial hosts log in with a password: choose a password credential.
credentialKeepPassword: Telnet or serial hosts log in with this credential, so it must stay a password.
quickStreamInvalid: Type telnet://[user@]host[:port], or serial://DEVICE with baud, data, parity and stop settings.
remindDaysBefore: {count, plural, one {# day before} other {# days before}}
noteHint: Notes are saved as plain text: do not put passwords here.
renewalNotifyNote: Show a system notification before a host's subscription renews, as many days ahead as the host's reminder.
backgroundNote: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 20 MB and 32 megapixels
backgroundUnsupported: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP image
backgroundTooLarge: The image exceeds 20 MB or 32 megapixels
hostKeyChanged: {host} presents a different host key from the one SSHYard saved. This is expected after the server is reinstalled or its SSH keys are regenerated; otherwise someone may be intercepting the connection.
hostKeyVerifyHint: Before trusting the new key, compare its fingerprint with the server's, for example by running ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub in the provider's web console.
knownHostsDesc: The host keys SSHYard trusts, kept in SSHYard's own file apart from ~/.ssh/known_hosts.
knownHostsEmpty: No host keys are trusted yet. SSHYard asks the first time it connects to a host.
knownHostsChanged: The known hosts file changed meanwhile. Try again.
hostKeyForgotten: Forgot the host key of {host}. SSHYard asks to trust it on the next connection.
broadcastBusy: The last command is still being sent, try again after it finishes
broadcastPlaceholder: Command for the selected terminals (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line)
broadcastConfirm: Each line may run as a command in the {count} selected terminals.
logRecordingCount: {count, plural, one {# terminal logging} other {# terminals logging}}
logNoTerminal: Open a terminal to log its session.
logNote: A log keeps, as text, what a terminal shows from the moment logging starts, commands echoed back included. Input it does not show, such as passwords, and full-screen programs such as vim are left out. A raw log keeps everything printed, full-screen programs included.
logSaveFailed: Could not save the terminal output: {error}
broadcastLiveNote: What you type in a selected terminal also goes to the other selected terminals
broadcastLiveOn: Keyboard input is synced to the selected terminals
broadcastPasteConfirm: The text has several lines; each may run as a command in the {count} synced terminals.
logFormatHint: Text keeps the lines as shown; raw keeps every byte printed, escape sequences included. Applies to logs started next.
logAuto: Log this host's terminals when they connect
logAutoHint: Each terminal of this host starts its session log as it connects, in the folder chosen in the Session Logs pane.
logRecentNone: No logs in this folder yet
historyNoSession: Open a terminal to see the commands run on its host.
historyStream: Command history needs SSH or a local shell. This pane is a Telnet or serial terminal.
historyNoTerminal: Open a terminal on this host to read its command history.
historyWSL: Command history of WSL shells is not supported yet.
historyNoneHint: No shell history file was found for this user. Bash writes its history when a shell exits.
historyShowMore: {count, plural, one {Show more (# left)} other {Show more (# left)}}

filesZoomNote: How large the names and rows of files panes show
sftpSudoOn: Open files as root with sudo
sftpSudoHint: Files panes run the server's sftp-server through sudo and can change any file. sudo gets the login password, or asks for one kept in memory for this run only.
sudoPasswordNeeded: sudo needs a password to open the files as root.
sudoNoServer: no sftp-server found on the server
challengeHint: Sent to the server for this login only, never saved.
errChallengeCanceled: Login to {host} was canceled: its verification questions were not answered.
errChallengeUnattended: {host} asks for a verification code or other input to log in, which this connection cannot ask. Connect from a terminal or files pane to enter it.
